cards.title: Savings
cards.blurb: Money kept safe for short-term needs, earning little growth.

cards.title: Investing
cards.blurb: Putting money to work so it can grow over a longer time.

cards.title: Inflation
cards.blurb: Rising prices mean idle cash slowly buys less over time.

cards.title: Mutual Fund
cards.blurb: Many people pool money into one fund run by professionals.

cards.title: Portfolio
cards.blurb: The full set of holdings a fund owns at a point in time.

cards.title: Fund Manager
cards.blurb: The professional who decides what the fund buys and sells.

cards.title: Diversification
cards.blurb: Spreading money across many holdings so one bad bet hurts less.

cards.title: NAV
cards.blurb: The price of one unit of a fund.

cards.title: Units
cards.blurb: Your share of a fund, bought at that day's NAV.

cards.title: Net Assets
cards.blurb: A fund's total value after what it owes, the base for its NAV.

cards.title: AMC
cards.blurb: The company that sets up and runs a fund house's schemes.

cards.title: Expense Ratio
cards.blurb: The yearly fee a fund takes from its value to cover running costs.

cards.title: Exit Load
cards.blurb: A fee charged if you sell units too soon after buying them.

cards.title: Direct vs Regular
cards.blurb: Direct plans skip distributor commission, so their fees are lower.

cards.title: Equity Fund
cards.blurb: A fund that mainly holds company shares, so its value swings more.

cards.title: Stock
cards.blurb: A small piece of ownership in one listed company.

cards.title: Market Cap
cards.blurb: The total market value of a company, used to compare firm sizes.

cards.title: Debt Fund
cards.blurb: A fund that lends money through bonds and similar instruments.

cards.title: Bond
cards.blurb: A loan you give a borrower, who pays interest and repays the amount.

cards.title: Rates vs Bonds
cards.blurb: When interest rates rise, existing bond prices usually fall.

cards.title: Market Index
cards.blurb: A basket of companies used to measure how a market is doing.

cards.title: Index Fund
cards.blurb: A fund that copies a market index instead of picking stocks itself.

cards.title: Rebalancing
cards.blurb: Resetting your mix back to target after markets move it.

cards.title: Riskometer
cards.blurb: The scale a fund uses to show how risky it is.

cards.title: Volatility
cards.blurb: How sharply a fund's value swings up and down over time.

cards.title: Time Horizon
cards.blurb: How long until you need the money, which shapes how much risk fits.

cards.title: Asset Allocation
cards.blurb: How you split money across equity, debt and other asset types.

cards.title: Goals First
cards.blurb: Decide what the money is for before picking any product.

cards.title: SIP
cards.blurb: Investing a fixed amount on a schedule.

cards.title: Lumpsum
cards.blurb: One large amount invested at once instead of in instalments.

cards.title: Small, Steady Wins
cards.blurb: Modest amounts, invested regularly, can add up to a lot.

cards.title: Cost Averaging
cards.blurb: Fixed sums buy more units when prices dip and fewer when they rise.

cards.title: Market Dip
cards.blurb: A temporary fall in prices, when a SIP buys more units.

cards.title: Fixed Amount
cards.blurb: The same sum invested each month, whatever the market is doing.

cards.title: Compounding
cards.blurb: Growth that earns its own growth.

cards.title: Rule of 72
cards.blurb: Divide 72 by the yearly return to estimate years to double money.

cards.title: Early Start
cards.blurb: Starting early gives compounding more years to do its work.

cards.title: Patience
cards.blurb: Long-term growth rewards staying put more than perfect timing.

cards.title: Stay Through Dips
cards.blurb: Staying invested through falls is how you catch the recovery.

cards.title: Panic Selling
cards.blurb: Selling in a fall can turn a temporary dip into a locked-in loss.
